summary: Riding a minecart cluster into a wall freezes the game
description: Derailed Minecarts that are clustered together often keep their movement speed, which is due to another bug (). In some cases (with the Minecart Improvements experiment enabled) if such clusters of minecarts are ridden by the player and collide with blocks, the screen goes black and the game stops working. It then has to be terminated manually. Steps to reproduce (or use the link below for a more reliable method): - Place around 20 to 30 minecarts on a normal rail. - Push the minecarts. They should now start to move off the rail, keeping their velocity. - Ride one of the minecarts in the cluster. - Wait until it collides into blocks (2 blocks high is best). Water like in the attached videos isn t needed. This is not very reliable, so a few attempts may be needed. Alternatively, the attached world ( ) can be used to reproduce the bug: - Open the world. - Walk into the minecart cluster. - Ride one of the minecarts in the cluster. - Wait until it collides into the wall and locks the game.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft.
2. Create a new Creative world with default settings.
3. Place around 20 to 30 minecarts on a normal rail.
4. Push the minecarts so they start to move off the rail, keeping their velocity.
5. Ride one of the minecarts in the cluster.
6. Wait until it collides into blocks (2 blocks high is best).
7. Observe that the screen goes black and the game stops working, requiring manual termination.
Observed Behavior: When a player rides a cluster of derailed minecarts that are moving at high speed and collides with a solid block, the game experiences a critical freeze, resulting in a black screen. This issue occurs specifically when the Minecart Improvements experiment is enabled, and it requires the player to manually terminate the game after the freeze. To reproduce this bug, one can place approximately 20 to 30 minecarts on a standard rail and push them to initiate movement, allowing them to maintain their velocity even after derailing. The player should then ride one of the minecarts in the cluster and wait for it to collide with a wall, preferably one that is two blocks high, to trigger the freeze. Although the presence of water is not necessary for this reproduction, achieving the freeze may require multiple attempts due to the unreliable nature of the bug. Alternatively, the issue can be tested using a provided world file, where the player can walk into the minecart cluster, ride one of the minecarts, and wait for the collision with the wall that causes the game to lock up.
Expected Behavior: When riding a cluster of minecarts, the player should be able to collide with blocks without causing the game to freeze or the screen to go black. Instead, the player should be ejected safely from the minecart upon impact, allowing for normal gameplay to continue without interruption. The minecarts should come to a stop or slow down appropriately, ensuring a smooth experience in Java Edition 1.21.4 and 1.21.5.
